237	**3.6 Correlation, pre-play, results, and the one resync rule (TR-pc-009, TR-pc-024, TR-shipbody-050).**
238	- **Correlation.** Every submit carries a non-zero `correlation` from a per-Adapter monotonic counter; the kernel echoes it unchanged in the terminal result (ADR-0002 § 7). The Adapter's `PrePlayLedger` is a preallocated ring (`PREPLAY_LEDGER_CAPACITY`, data) of `{correlation, kind, pre-play token, frame}` entries, where `kind` is a command type index or one of the two intent kinds; intents carry a correlation so that a rejection can be attributed to a kind, because the result record has no type field.
239	- **Pre-play is body and sound only, never the effect, never the beam light.** The Adapter records a token (the hand's switch animation, the tool click, the bar starting) in the ledger; the Avatar Presenter and Audio read the token list through `AdapterViews` and draw or play it. Light and effects change only on committed state (ADR-0009 § 7; kernel anti-target: no client-side prediction at MVP). A result for an *immediate* reason (the reason class is declared by Interaction's table, ADR-0020; the Adapter calls its pure `ReasonClass.is_immediate(reason)`) withdraws the token within one frame; a `PRECONDITION` outcome is an `Applied` command and is never withdrawn; a `Superseded` or `Dropped` result withdraws silently; a token without a result is withdrawn at `PREPLAY_MAX_TICKS`. The ack frame of a command whose channel will complete and of one that will resolve to `PRECONDITION` is the same token and therefore pixel-identical.
240	- **Result handler.** The result handler is a method `Callable` on the Adapter (ADR-0002 § 1: no lambda), registered with `SurfaceHandle.set_result_handler` and cleared in `_exit_tree`. It copies the record's scalars into a fixed `ResultRing` and returns `ctx.complete()`; every consequence (withdraw a token, schedule a resync) happens in the next `_process` (ADR-0009 § 7).
241	- **No shared or assisted control.** There is one Adapter, one local PlayerId and one seat; a command whose `issuer_peer` does not own the actor is `Rejected(ACTOR_NOT_OWNED)` at P2 with no state change (ADR-0002 § 4), and the Adapter has no code path that submits for an actor other than `actor_of_seat(local_player)`.
242	- **The resync rule: one mechanism, five labelled triggers.** The Adapter keeps `last_acked` per intent kind (`UNKNOWN` initially). A **resync** sets `last_acked := UNKNOWN`, which makes the next sample's value differ and so bypasses the change filter exactly once; the resend is rate-limited to one per `AIM_SEND_INTERVAL` ticks per kind so a persistent rejection cannot flood. For a hold-mode channel it also compares the real state of `interact` with the last submitted one and submits `cancel_channel` if the button is up. The triggers, each with its observable source:
243	
244	| # | Trigger | Observed from | Notes |
245	|---|---|---|---|
246	| i | An intent result arrives not-ok (`STALE` is the case that matters; any not-ok other than `DEAD` and `NOT_ACCEPTING` counts) | the `ResultRing` | D.7: `last_acked` is "set on submit, reverted on any rejection" |
247	| ii | The kernel leaves `PAUSED` | `PresentationClock.state` changed from `PAUSED` to `RUNNING` | the kernel rejects intents immediately while paused, so a release during the pause was lost |
248	| iii | `LOADING -> RUNNING` | `PresentationClock.load_seq` changed | a restore or a new game |
249	| iv | Window focus returns, or the active pad reconnects | focus notification latch; `joy_connection_changed` latch | § 3.7 |
250	| v | `TRANSFER`: the actor's `body_of_actor` changed | `BodyView.body_of_actor(actor)` differs from the last seen | a pod arrival, a section detach |

252	Triggers ii and iii are one code path: the Adapter resyncs on the first frame in which it observes `RUNNING` after any frame that was not `RUNNING`, and labels the cause for the `PC_RESYNC` counter. **Why this lands in P2 of the first post-restore tick (TR-shipbody-050):** the frame that carries the kernel into `RUNNING` clears the accumulator and discards its own delta, so it runs no tick (ADR-0001 § 6; architecture.md Data Flow 1); the Adapter, which runs at -100 before the driver, has not yet seen that frame's end state, observes the new `load_seq` at the start of the next frame, and submits its resync before the driver runs that frame's first tick; the commands enter that tick's P1 batch and apply in its P2. Body's `sub` therefore survives the restore if a key is still held and is reset once by a later resync only in the case the rule gives (at most one sub-pixel remainder lost); a restore with no key held resets `sub` as a stop does. The invariant is testable: the simulation's intent equals the player's hands within one tick of the kernel being `RUNNING`.

263	**3.9 What the Adapter publishes: `AdapterViews`.** A presentation-local, getter-only object (`src/presentation/controller/input/adapter_views.gd`, a `RefCounted` held by the composition root and handed read-only to the Avatar Presenter, HUD, Instruments, Audio and the Chart Table layer). 265	### 4. Input contexts (TR-pc-010, TR-pc-033, TR-hud-041, TR-instr-032, TR-charttable-012)
266	
267	**4.1 The machine.** `InputContextMachine` (pure; Adapter-local; never persisted, never in a snapshot) holds exactly one of `GAMEPLAY`, `CHART_TABLE`, `INSPECT_CARD`, `CHAT` (VS-B). Before a campaign is loaded the Adapter runs in `CHART_TABLE` with no gameplay sink, publishing the same MenuInput stream (PC-2a); the first `RUNNING` frame after a new game or load enters `GAMEPLAY`. The sim state is unchanged by a context change except through the zero intent and the cancel the Adapter submits on entry.
268	
269	**4.2 The matrix is data; the transitions are code with tests.** `context_matrix.json` carries, per action family and context, one of the policies of § 3.5, copied from the GDD's context × action matrix and checked at boot for completeness (every family has a row in every context). The context return table of the GDD is the closed set of transitions in `InputContextMachine.step`, covered one test per row:
270	- Entering any non-`GAMEPLAY` context submits `set_move_intent {NONE}` and clears the run latch. Entering `CHART_TABLE` or `CHAT` also submits `cancel_channel` for a hold-mode or a toggle-mode channel (in the co-op overlay the sim runs, so a channel the player cannot see must not keep burning). **Entering `INSPECT_CARD` does not cancel** (the Pillar 4 second-instrument check on the pipe being welded is free): the zeroed move intent is not a move, the channel continues, a held `interact` is still tracked in hold mode, and a release inside the card still cancels; `cancel` closes the card first and a second `cancel` cancels the channel.
271	- **Movement closes the card** (user ruling D94): a *fresh* movement input in `INSPECT_CARD` (a move key going down, or the left stick crossing `MOVE_DEADZONE` from below `MOVE_DEADZONE - MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT`, plus `CARD_PAD_DEADZONE_MARGIN` on a pad) returns to `GAMEPLAY` and submits the first `set_move_intent` of that octant **in the same frame, in that order**. A direction already held at card entry is latched until released. A move that closes the card while a channel runs is an ordinary non-NONE intent and aborts the channel in the sim, as in `GAMEPLAY`.
272	- A published `loco_state` of STAGGERED, DOWNED, DEAD or IN_POD returns any context to `GAMEPLAY` on the frame the Adapter observes it (it polls `ControllerView.loco_state` once per frame; every one of those states lasts well over a frame), and the cursor hides again. `chart_table` and `request_pause` are Adapter-level and never gated by `loco_state`, so pause stays reachable in DOWNED.
273	- `INSPECT_CARD`: `set_aim` stays live (the lamp can hold the gauge lit), zoom is live, `chart_table` closes the card first with no pause on that press, and `CHART_TABLE` is never entered from `INSPECT_CARD`.
274	
275	**4.3 Latch-until-released.** For any physical control whose press closed the layer (Resume accept, `chart_table`, `cancel`) the Adapter emits nothing from that control, to the layer or to gameplay, until it is physically released and pressed again, including across the `PAUSED -> RUNNING` resync; for a console press that opened the layer, the open press's release and repeats are latched the same way, so no `interact` edge can reach `pod_hop` until a fresh press (TR-charttable-012). The latch set is Adapter state keyed by control, cleared by the matching release record in the `EdgeRing`.
276	
277	**4.4 Cursor policy (TR-pc-033, TR-hud-041).** `CursorPolicy.mode_for(context)` is a pure table: `GAMEPLAY` and `INSPECT_CARD` -> `MOUSE_MODE_CONFINED_HIDDEN` (hidden and confined; in `INSPECT_CARD` it stays hidden and **inert**: the mouse still steers aim and picks nothing on the card, because a visible cursor would be a second pointer over the beam); `CHART_TABLE`, `CHAT` and the boot context -> `MOUSE_MODE_VISIBLE` (shown and released), with the shape taken from the layer's `cursor_hint` (DEFAULT or SELECTABLE). `EngineInputSource` applies the mode only on a change. HUD nodes in `GAMEPLAY` have `mouse_filter` IGNORE and `focus_mode` NONE and no gamepad focus is ever assigned to a HUD node; that node-flag half of TR-hud-041 is ADR-0030's. The cursor is hidden by mode, so no custom cursor image exists and `aim_indicator` (opt-in, off by default) is a HUD overlay.
278	
279	### 5. The MenuInput stream (TR-pc-012, TR-charttable-010, TR-charttable-036)
280	
281	The Adapter publishes a presentation-local event stream while the active context is `CHART_TABLE` (and in the boot context). It is a `MenuInputQueue`: a preallocated ring of parallel `PackedInt32Array` columns (`kind`, `a`, `b`, `x`, `y`; capacity `MENU_EVENT_CAPACITY`, data), so it allocates nothing per event and carries no object. Kinds are the registry's `menu_input_stream` set: `NAV_DOWN{dir, source}` and `NAV_UP{dir}` (`dir` UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT; `source` STICK, DPAD, ARROW, WASD), `ACCEPT_DOWN`, `ACCEPT_UP`, `BACK`, `CLOSE`, `FOCUS_OUT`, `FOCUS_IN`, `DEVICE_CHANGED{device}` and `POINTER{kind MOVE/DOWN/UP/WHEEL, button, x, y}`.
282	
283	- **Sampling and delivery.** Events are produced in the Adapter's `_process` at -100 from the ordered `EdgeRing`; the Chart Table layer, a layer 3 and 4 UI object that runs on engine time so that it responds while the kernel is `PAUSED` (ADR-0009 § 3, ADR-0008 § 6.3) and always after the Adapter in the same frame, drains the queue at the start of its update and calls `clear()`. All events of one render frame therefore arrive in arrival order before the layer's update (ADR-0030 consumes this). An undrained queue is cleared at the next Adapter frame and counted (`PC_MENU_DROPPED`). On a full queue the Adapter drops the newest event, counts `PC_MENU_OVERFLOW` and enqueues one `FOCUS_OUT` on the next frame, which every consumer treats as "release all holds and clear navigation", so an overflow can lose a press but can never wedge a hold.
284	- **What the Adapter owns (PC-2a (a) to (g)).** Echo suppression (echo records are ignored, § 3.2); deadzone hysteresis (a stick takes a NAV edge on crossing `MOVE_DEADZONE` from below `MOVE_DEADZONE - MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT` and releases below that band); the cardinal-axis rule (one NAV direction at a time, the larger axis, a tie to the vertical, changing only after the stick re-passes the exit band); latch-until-released (§ 4.3); `FOCUS_OUT` releases every held menu control and the layer's hold fills abort, `FOCUS_IN` requires fresh presses; `DEVICE_CHANGED` follows the device latch (§ 3.3); the cursor hint is applied by `EngineInputSource`, its only `Input` caller. Accept is the physical controls of `interact` in this context minus every mouse button, plus Enter and Space as fixed extra keyboard accepts of this context; **a mouse button is only ever a `POINTER` event, never an `ACCEPT`**. Back is `cancel`, close is `chart_table`. Auto-repeat of a held NAV direction is the layer's (Chart Table D.9). `zoom_in` and `zoom_out` edges are never emitted here.
285	- **Pointer position.** `POINTER` carries the root-viewport mouse position as integer physical window pixels, forwarded unconverted: root stretch is disabled (ADR-0008 § 5), so no inverse stretch transform applies. The layer subtracts `RenderLayout.picture_rect.position` itself (the HUD origin) and maps to HUD pixels and art pixels; the Adapter's aim path subtracts the world picture's origin exactly once through `RenderLayout.mouse_to_world_aim` (§ 6.1); each consumer subtracts once and the stream value is never subtracted twice. That the unit is window pixels on a real letterboxed window is confirmed by PC-INPUT-SPIKE-1 (a) (AC-CT-135 (f)).
286	- **No gameplay in the stream.** It carries no command and no simulation read, and the layer submits nothing and reads no device (TR-charttable-010); the console seam (§ 3.8) is the only route from the layer's state into a payload, and it goes through the Adapter.
287	
288	### 6. The aim path, the cursor and the zoom edge
289	
290	**6.1 Raw aim, once per frame, from the open-loop mapping (TR-pc-031, TR-pxl-014).** In its `_process` the Adapter forms, for the local avatar, one raw aim:
291	1. `cursor_px: Vector2i = InputSource.cursor_px()`: the root viewport's mouse position, converted once with `floori` per axis (that it is integral, or fractional under display scaling, is PC-INPUT-SPIKE-1 (a); if it is fractional, the single `floori` is the one place the cursor is quantised).
292	2. `world: Vector2 = pipeline.layout.mouse_to_world_aim(cursor_px, pipeline.f_q)` (ADR-0008 § 3.3: `f_q + (cursor_px - picture_centre) / k_z`, with the single picture-origin subtraction **inside** that method). The Adapter does not form `cursor_vp` itself and subtracts nothing, so the letterbox subtraction exists in exactly one place; the GDD's alternative of subtracting in the Adapter is not used.
293	3. `r = world - Vector2(floor(pos_curr) + Vector2i(0, AIM_ORIGIN_Y))` with `pos_curr` from Body's published view (the committed tick's position). If `|r| < AIM_MOUSE_DEADZONE_PX` the raw aim holds. Otherwise `theta = atan2(-r.y, r.x)` and `aim_q = posmod(roundi(theta * AIM_UNITS / TAU), AIM_UNITS)`: **round once, then `posmod`** (the lower half-plane would otherwise go negative; D.7's worked values 764, 3332, 3072, 4095 are the unit-test vectors). The result is an `int`; the float never reaches `submit`.
294	
295	`mouse_to_world_view`, which maps through `pose_q` and therefore includes the look-ahead `L`, **never feeds aim** (a loop: aim moves the camera, the camera moves the world point under a still cursor, which moves aim). Rule `CTL-06` (§ 8.2) bans the name inside the aim path. Because the Adapter runs at -100, before `PipelineRoot._process` at 0, the `f_q`, `layout` and `layout_version` it reads are the **previous frame's** `CAMERA_SOLVE` and `RESCALING` results and `pos_curr` is the last committed tick: one coherent snapshot, a frame old, which is the lag the GDD already costs into the recorded trade-off (a still mouse turns the beam by the geometry of the follow-lag change when a run starts or stops, bounded by the GDD's 36 px).
296	
297	**6.2 Sources.** `aim_source` ∈ {AUTO, MOUSE, STICK, KEYS} is an `InputSettings` value (Settings, never sim). The right stick uses the scaled-radial deadzone (`AIM_DEADZONE`, `AIM_OUTER`, `AIM_CURVE`) and the released-stick modes of PC-5; the four arrow keys and `aim_hold` compose an octant-centre aim (`512 * o`). `live` is true for the mouse always, for a stick above its deadzone, for a key while held, and false under `FOLLOW_ALWAYS`; it travels in the payload because facing rules 4 to 6 branch on it in the sim.
298	
299	**6.3 The cursor warp (a presentation-local rule; submits nothing, writes no block, reveals no sim state).** The OS cursor is hidden and confined in `GAMEPLAY`, so the Adapter may reposition it unseen:
300	- **Zoom edge.** The Adapter stores `cursor_off` (the cursor relative to the picture centre, in base pixels, from the frame's aim computation) every frame. A zoom step is accepted inside `PipelineRoot._process` of frame N and bumps `layout_version`. In frame N+1 the Adapter sees the version change, **uses the stored `cursor_off` as that frame's aim input instead of a fresh OS read**, and warps the hidden cursor to `picture_centre_new + cursor_off * k_new` (clamped to the window), so `aim_q` is unchanged within one unit while the avatar is still. The cost is that one frame of mouse motion is dropped on a warp frame (at most one rendered frame, 17 ms at 60 fps). Whether the OS position is readable in the same frame after `warp_mouse`, and whether the warp emits a synthetic motion event that would be double counted, are PC-INPUT-SPIKE-1 (b); if the warped position is readable immediately the "use the stored offset" step is dropped.
301	- **Handover to the mouse.** While the source is STICK or KEYS the mouse takes over only after `AIM_MOUSE_TAKEOVER_PX` of accumulated cursor travel, and at takeover the cursor is first warped to the point whose direction from the aim origin is the current raw aim and whose radius is the larger of the last radius and `AIM_WARP_RADIUS_PX`, so the first mouse sample holds the aim it found. `AUTO` follows the last aim axis; a forced source ignores the others and has no handover warp.
302	- A **fresh** mouse motion after a focus return or a context change is not a warp trigger.
303	
304	**6.4 Zoom and the pipeline root (TR-pc-032, TR-pxl-032, TR-pc-033).** `zoom_in` and `zoom_out` are the Adapter's two edge-triggered inputs (PC-16). The wheel notches latched in a frame are summed to a net sign and the Adapter calls `PipelineRoot.request_zoom_step(sign)` **at most once per rendered frame** (a notched or high-resolution wheel cannot walk the ladder several steps in one frame); a pad d-pad press is the same call. The call is host-local and never a command; the rate limit and the ladder are ADR-0008's (`ZOOM_STEP_MIN_INTERVAL`, one accepted step per frame). Zoom is live in `GAMEPLAY` and `INSPECT_CARD` and ignored in `CHART_TABLE` and `CHAT`. **The pipeline root makes no `Input` read of its own.** TR-pc-032's "the Adapter hands cursor position and zoom edges to the pipeline root" is met in the form that needs no new `PipelineRoot` interface: zoom edges are the `request_zoom_step` call, and the cursor is published as `AdapterViews.cursor_px()` for any presenter that needs a pick, which converts it through the `RenderLayout` methods. The wheel burst size per frame is PC-INPUT-SPIKE-1 (c).
305	
306	### 7. The Avatar Presenter
307	
308	**7.1 Registration and reads.** `AvatarPresenter` registers a `PresenterDescriptor` at `PresentationStage.AVATAR` (2) with no `_process` (ADR-0009 § 3); its `present(frame)` reads `body.state` previous and current positions and the odometer, `ControllerView` (facing, `gait_effective`, `octant`, `loco_state`, `carry_ref`, chest and hand points, `stagger_end_tick`, `t_downed`), `emitter.state` (beam lit and shape) and `frame.alpha`, and places everything with `Placement.at` and `Placement.put` (ADR-0009 § 4: interpolate, then floor per axis, so every written position has a zero fractional part). It draws any crewmate, local or remote, from the same views with no HOST/MIRROR branch (CR-10). For the **local avatar only** it also reads the Adapter's `raw_aim()` to rotate the chest `Light2D` (the drawn cone may lead the committed cone by at most `AIM_SEND_THRESHOLD` and one send interval, the accepted divergence of PC-5); a remote avatar's beam rotates from the replicated committed `aim_angle`, which may not be coarsened below the facing hysteresis. The pre-play tokens of `AdapterViews` drive the hand's switch animation only. The Presenter keeps its `anim_counter` private.

310	*Frame index.* Moving frames are `posmod(anim_counter, 8)` with `anim_counter` accumulating `dir * (cycle_pos - cycle_pos_prev)` from Body's `odometer` (D.11); the cadence test samples the Presenter once per tick through an injected `PresentFrame`, so the accumulator sees the same odometer sequence at every render rate. **The tick-stepped frames are derived from the committed tick `T`**, not from `present_time`. *Idle breathing* is free-running: `AvatarFrames.idle_frame(T)` is `posmod(floor(T / IDLE_FRAME_TICKS), 6)` with no entry tick (the GDD's `T - T_enter` needs a per-state entry tick that the block does not hold and that a catch-up frame cannot observe exactly; a breath that starts mid-cycle is invisible; GDD sync). *Work, stagger and down frames* are anchored on a sim-held entry tick through `AvatarFrames.timed_frame(T, enter_tick, ticks_per_frame, n, one_shot)`: stagger on `stagger_end_tick - STAGGER_TICKS`, down on `t_downed` (both published by the view), and the work loop on the **channel's start tick published by Interaction** (assumption on ADR-0020: the channel record carries it), so a weld animation always starts at its first frame and the GDD's work formula is unchanged. Carry-idle is the static carry frame 0 and needs no clock. Because `T` does not advance while the kernel is `PAUSED`, these freeze under pause with no special case (TR-pc-038), and because they are a pure function of committed ticks they are identical across render cadences (TR-pc-039). **This is an exception to the registry pattern `cosmetic_phase_from_tick_counter`** ("cosmetic phase uses `present_time`, never the tick counter"), which ADR-0001 and ADR-0009 own. It is a deliberate, narrow one: only `AvatarFrames`, only for the avatar's tick-stepped frames, whose per-tick output must replay byte-identically. It is a foundation ask (below) and the pattern is mechanically unlinted today (ADR-0010 § 6.6b: "No lint"), so the exception is enforced by review and by the avatar cadence test. The moving frames are driven by Body's `odometer`, a simulation value, so they need no exception; every other cosmetic (flicker, fade, the ignored-input cue) keeps `present_time`.

320	**8.1 The Input allow-list (TR-pc-032).** `tools/lint/config/allowlists/input_surface.json` is the `READ-01` entry (ADR-0010 § 6.6: each entry `{path_glob, symbol, reason, owner, added}`). The symbols `Input`, `InputMap`, `InputEvent` (and every `InputEvent*` subclass name), `_input`, `_unhandled_input`, `_unhandled_key_input`, `_shortcut_input` may appear only in:
321	`src/presentation/controller/input/input_adapter.gd`, `engine_input_source.gd`, `binding_factory.gd`, `raw_event.gd`, and `dev_actions.gd` (dev feature tag only; excluded from the release export). Tests under `tests/` and `addons/gdUnit4/` are outside the rule. `Control.gui_input` and `_gui_input` are not on the list and are not banned by this ADR; ADR-0030 may request an entry by amendment if a layer needs one. 322	
323	**8.2 Controller lint pack `tools/lint/controller_lint.gd` (rule ids `CTL-nn`, ADR-0010 § 6.1 to § 6.7 mechanism, each with bad and good fixtures).**
324	
325	| Rule | Statement | Source | Tier |
326	|---|---|---|---|
327	| CTL-01 | The Adapter writes no block: in `src/presentation/controller/` none of `open_for(`, `WriteScope`, `mark_dirty(`, `register_block(`, `ModuleFacet`, `Command.new(`, and no import edge to `src/sim/controller/` internals (only `views/`) | TR-pc-001; ARCH-02 matrix | E2 |
328	| CTL-02 | `.device` is never compared with an integer literal or a `DEVICE_ID_*` constant (`==`, `!=`, `<`, `>`, `in`, `match`) anywhere in `src/` and `tools/`; a comparison with a variable is allowed | TR-pc-011, TR-pxl-032; engine 4.7 | E2 |
329	| CTL-03 | `mass_g`, `instance_mass_g`, `weight_class`, `salvage_yield` do not appear in `src/sim/controller/` or `src/presentation/controller/` | TR-boarding-007 | E2 |
330	| CTL-04 | No symbol naming a `ControllerRow` field is written outside `src/sim/controller/`; the four mutators are the only cross-block write path | TR-pc-018 | E2 |

341	**8.3 Behavioural tests (gdUnit4, headless, a `FakeInputSource`).** One test per row of the context return table; the context matrix completeness check; octant and aim quantiser vectors including the lower half-plane; the send predicate and the 26 commands a second bound; the resync with each of the five triggers (and the labelled counter); a press during a channel is submitted and answered `BUSY` with nothing queued; `set_move_intent` before any command in one frame; a stop and a `begin_*` in one frame; focus loss and pad loss; the console seam with and without a pick; `tool_cycle` with two presses in one frame; the confirm bar under a 1 s frame, under `PAUSED` and across a pause; `BindingFactory` output has `device == BINDING_ANY_DEVICE` on every event; the field-agreement test of § 8.4; `snapshot(restore(snapshot()))` byte identity from every rest value and from a live DOWNED row; a restore with the cap at WALK_ONLY does not stagger; the `FULL -> NONE -> WALK_ONLY -> FULL -> WALK_ONLY` sequence staggers once; the `controller.step` order tests; `Rejected(ACTOR_NOT_OWNED)` for a foreign actor; a DEAD seat rejects every Controller command and the Adapter submits nothing.

Adding a field means editing the one list and the test fails until all four agree.

345	**8.5 The input-trace format (TR-pc-039, replay half).** An `InputTrace` (`src/presentation/controller/input/input_trace.gd`, recorded only under the dev feature tag; replayed by `FakeInputSource`) is a text file of integer records, one line per rendered frame, committed under `tests/fixtures/controller/traces/` and immutable once committed. Header: a format version and the tick-rate name. Per frame: the injected `delta_us` (ADR-0001/ADR-0005's replay injection), the integer action strengths in `ANALOG_UNITS`, the ordered edge records of that frame (`action_id`, pressed, device class, echo), the wheel net sign, the cursor `Vector2i`, the pipeline values the Adapter read (`layout_version`, `f_q`, `k_z`, picture rect), the kernel state and `load_seq`, the focus flag and the pad-connected flag. Per-frame placements vary with alpha by design (ADR-0009). Hold-to-confirm timings are render-time by D.10 and are excluded from the identical claim: a confirm submit may land one frame apart across cadences.

347	**8.6 Budgets (TR-pc-029).** Advisory, measured by the diagnostics timer on a release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK, 120-frame warm-up, owned by the technical-director and living in `tests/performance/controller/`; a miss logs and never fails a logic test: Adapter at most 0.1 ms per frame (sampling, quantising, focus scoring over 32 candidates, submitting); `LocomotionStep` at most 0.05 ms per actor per tick against 2,000 rects (Body's, ADR-0015); `controller.step` at most 0.02 ms per actor per tick; Avatar Presenter at most 0.1 ms per avatar per frame; the `PC_*` diagnostics at most 0.01 ms per tick (dev only).

425	### Implementation Guidelines
426	- **Must** keep `Input.*`, `InputMap`, `InputEvent*`, `_input`, `_unhandled_input`, `_unhandled_key_input` and `_shortcut_input` inside the files of `input_surface.json`; **must never** read a device from the Chart Table layer, the pipeline root, HUD, Instruments or the Presenter.
427	- **Must** submit only from `InputAdapter._process`, in the order `set_move_intent`, `set_aim`, commands; **must never** submit from `_input`, a signal handler, `_physics_process` or while `PresentationClock.state` is not `RUNNING`.
428	- **Must** convert every analogue value to an `int` in `ANALOG_UNITS` and every position to `Vector2i` at the `InputSource` boundary; **must never** let a float reach `submit()`.
429	- **Must** build every binding with `physical_keycode` for keys and `device = BINDING_ANY_DEVICE`; **must** register every action before the first poll; **must never** compare `InputEvent.device` with a literal or a `DEVICE_ID_*` constant.
430	- **Must** send `set_move_intent` only on change or resync; **must** send `set_aim` on the D.7 predicate at most once per `AIM_SEND_INTERVAL` ticks; **must never** buffer a press (`ACTION_BUFFER_TICKS` is 0).
431	- **Must** attach a non-zero `correlation` to every submit and key pre-play tokens by it; **must never** pre-play an effect or the beam light.
432	- **Must** compute mouse aim only as `mouse_to_world_aim(cursor_px, f_q)` then round once and `posmod`; **must never** use `mouse_to_world_view` or `pose_q` for aim, and **must never** subtract the picture origin in the Adapter.
433	- **Must** hold the context, `last_acked`, hold timers, run latch, device latch, pre-play tokens and menu latch in Adapter classes that the Controller Sim cannot name; **must never** put any of them in `controller.state` or a snapshot.
434	- **Must** register `controller.state`, the four commands and the two hooks only through the `ModuleFacet.registrar` in `BOOTING`; **must** end every kernel-invoked callable in `return ctx.complete()`; **must never** write a `controller.state` field except in the Controller's own callables and the four mutators.
435	- **Must** keep `ControllerSchema.fields()` the single list and the agreement test green; **must never** persist a derived value (`chest_sim`, `hand_sim`) or a `Vector2i`.
436	- **Must** clear only `channel_ref`, `channel_face` and `channel_body` on a body edge; **must never** write a `body.state` field from the Controller.
437	- **Must** draw avatar tick-stepped loops from `AvatarFrames` on the committed tick; **must never** use that tick for any other cosmetic, and **must never** clamp a chest or hand point at run time.
438	- **Must** read only `locomotion_cap` and `stowed_heavy` from Suit in the Controller Sim and no Sanity, Attention or `PERCEPTION_OUT` view anywhere in the module.
439	
440	## Alternatives Considered
441	
442	### Alternative 1: One `Controller` node that reads devices, owns the state and draws the body
443	- **Description**: A single `Node2D` (or autoload) reads `Input`, holds facing, gait and carry in its own fields, and moves the sprite.

This confirms a real problem: with a deadzone of 0.0, setting up an action via InputMap.add_action makes any pad-axis-bound action report as pressed even at rest, since centered events trigger both directions and resting triggers register as pressed. That means edge-detection logic combining event_is_action with is_action_pressed would generate false press edges.

My fix is to use the default deadzone (around 0.2-0.5) for all actions and avoid relying on is_action_pressed for stick-bound actions entirely—the Adapter should read raw strength independent of deadzone, and treat axis-bound inputs like JoypadMotion as continuous rather than edge-triggered, using hysteresis on raw strength for things like menu navigation instead of event latching. I've verified raw strength reads correctly even for tiny values in mixed scenarios, so next I want to check abstract class forms, set_input_as_handled on Node, const arrays, Vector2i flooring, and _input call ordering.

content.content:
### Alternative 1: One `Controller` node that reads devices, owns the state and draws the body
- **Description**: A single `Node2D` (or autoload) reads `Input`, holds facing, gait and carry in its own fields, and moves the sprite.
- **Pros**: Least code; no read views; no resync because there is no boundary.
- **Cons**: State lives in the scene tree, so a save cannot restore it and a MIRROR peer cannot draw a remote body from state; presentation would write the simulation (kernel H4); the simulation would depend on a `Node` (ADR-0010 `SIM-01`); input timing would be the scene's, not the tick's.
- **Rejection Reason**: Breaks three Foundation rules and the GDD's PC-1 rationale; the three-part split is the minimum that satisfies them.

### Alternative 2: Fold the Controller Sim into Ship Body (one block, one hook)
- **Description**: Body owns intent, gait, facing and position; the Controller is only an Adapter and a Presenter.
- **Pros**: One fewer block and hook; no `controller.step` -> `body.integrate` ordering edge.
- **Cons**: Intent and facing are seat semantics (what the player asked for) read by Interaction, Attention, Horror and the HUD; position is a kinematic fact. Merging them couples every reader of the first to Body's schema and its restore rules, and the GDD rejected it for that reason (PC-1 rationale).
- **Rejection Reason**: Keeping the input record apart from the integrator keeps both restore contracts small; the cost is one hook edge, which the topo-sort already handles.

### Alternative 3: The Controller owns position and calls the Layout projection
- **Description**: `controller.step` integrates the foot box against Layout's rectangles.
- **Pros**: One owner for "where the player is".
- **Cons**: Puts the Layout projection inside an input system; cannot own an actor that transfers between bodies (pod hop, detach) without learning Body's rebase rules; Horror's reuse of `LocomotionStep` would have to reach into the Controller.
- **Rejection Reason**: PC-14's reasons; the composite ship and the transfer mutators are Body's.

### Alternative 4: Per-tick held-state commands instead of change-based intents
- **Description**: The Adapter submits the current octant and aim every tick; no change filter, no `last_acked`, no resync.
- **Pros**: Self-healing; no resync rule; the simulation can never disagree with the hands for more than a tick.
- **Cons**: A steady 60 or more commands a second against `MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK` and the `var_to_bytes` size check, for a state that is constant most of the time; the command log and the replay trace would be dominated by repeats; ADR-0002's coalescing exists for exactly the bursty case, not a firehose.
- **Rejection Reason**: Change-based submission with one resync rule has the same invariant (hands equal intent within a tick of `RUNNING`) at one fiftieth of the traffic, and the five triggers are all observable.

### Alternative 5: Poll-only edges, or latch in `_unhandled_input`
- **Description**: Use `is_action_just_pressed` and `just_released` for every edge; or latch events in `_unhandled_input`.
- **Pros**: Poll-only is the simplest code and needs no ring. `_unhandled_input` leaves `Control`s first refusal.
- **Cons**: Probe 6: a same-frame press and release cannot be ordered by polling, which the latch-until-released, fresh-press and hold-cancel rules need. `_unhandled_input` misses an event a focused `Control` consumed, which would silently drop a MenuInput accept.
- **Rejection Reason**: Ordered edges from `_input`, plus a poll for continuous state, is the smallest scheme that is correct for all three; the cost is the `EdgeRing`.

### Alternative 6: A custom binding layer instead of `InputMap`
- **Description**: The Adapter matches raw `InputEventKey`/`JoypadButton` records against its own table; no `InputMap` actions.
- **Pros**: No dependence on `InputMap` device semantics (probe 3); total control of conflicts and contexts.
- **Cons**: Re-implements modifier matching, axis deadzones, echo and per-device merging that the engine already provides; the HUD, Settings and accessibility screens would each need the custom layer; Godot's merging of devices per action (a held pad `interact` survives a touch of the mouse) would have to be rebuilt.
- **Rejection Reason**: `InputMap` with runtime registration, zero engine deadzone and the any-device wildcard gives the same control with the engine's matching; the pitfall (probe 3) is closed by one factory and one test.

### Alternative 7: Mouse aim through the camera pose (`mouse_to_world_view`) or anchored on the avatar
- **Description**: Use the full `pose_q` inverse for aim, or measure aim from the drawn avatar position.
- **Pros**: Matches picking and pings; the anchored form holds the beam rigid against the hand.
- **Cons**: `pose_q` contains the look-ahead `L`, which is a function of aim, so a still cursor would drift the beam (a feedback loop with no cursor drawn to explain it). Anchoring on the avatar puts the hidden-cursor reference up to the follow lag plus the look-ahead off the drawn avatar (GDD PC-5, ruling R4).
- **Rejection Reason**: The open-loop `f_q` form is the ruled one and ADR-0008 publishes it; the lint `CTL-06` keeps the loop open.

### Alternative 8: Identify devices by number (`device == 0`, or the `DEVICE_ID_*` constants)
- **Description**: Decide keyboard, mouse or pad from `event.device`.
- **Pros**: One integer compare.
- **Cons**: 4.7 changed the keyboard and mouse numbers and some pads already used 0 (`modules/input.md`); pads are numbered by enumeration order, so a pad that is not first matches nothing; a comparison with a constant bakes the engine's numbering into game code.
- **Rejection Reason**: Event type is stable across versions; the only legal numeric use is a variable holding the active pad's index, never a literal.

### Alternative 9: Persist the context, `last_acked` and the pre-play ledger
- **Description**: Save Adapter state so a load resumes mid-intent.
- **Pros**: A restore could keep the exact held input.
- **Cons**: The hands are the source of truth, not the save; a persisted `last_acked` would claim the simulation holds a value it just lost; the context is presentation. It would also put device state into a hashed block.
- **Rejection Reason**: The restore normalises transient fields and the resync re-sends the real hands (TR-pc-021).

## Consequences

### Positive
- Only five files can read a device; every other Controller file is pure over ints, so the Adapter's logic is unit-testable with a scripted source and replayable from a recorded trace.
- The Adapter cannot write the simulation by construction (no `ModuleFacet`, a `PresentationFacet` of class `INPUT_SURFACE`, an import-edge matrix that stops at `views/`), and the Controller Sim cannot read a device (no `Input` token is legal under `src/sim/`).
- One field list drives the block, the view and the snapshot, so the three cannot drift; a new field is one edit and one failing test until the rest follow.
- The 4.7 device-id change is closed twice: by classification on event type and by a literal-compare lint; the wildcard binding closes the pad-index hazard the probes found.
- Resync is one mechanism with five labelled causes, all observable from the clock, the result ring, the notifications and Body's view, with no kernel hook.
- Hold, toggle, pad and keyboard policies differ only in when the Adapter submits two commands the owners already define.
- Intent submission is ten to fifty times lighter than per-tick held state and stays inside the 26 commands a second budget.

### Negative
- Adapter state is lost on a restore and rebuilt from the hands; a player holding a key across a load gets one resend, at most one sub-pixel `sub` remainder, and no more.
- The Adapter reads the previous frame's `f_q` and layout (it runs before the pipeline), so aim and the zoom warp carry one frame of lag, and a warp frame drops one frame of mouse motion.
- Edge ordering needs an `EdgeRing` and a second path beside polling; the lint and fixtures to keep that honest are real work.
- The avatar's tick-stepped frames (idle, work, stagger, down) use the committed tick, an exception to a registry rule that must be defended in review and by test, because no lint can see it.
- Four Controller mutators are Class A in ADR-0003's vocabulary while the GDD says Class B; two documents must be amended.
- The Presenter and Audio share one pure function, which makes `AvatarFrames` a small cross-presentation contract that must stay stable.

## Risks
- **R1. Process order on a release export is unverified (KRN-LAT-02).** If the Adapter does not run before the driver, an intent sampled in frame N lands a tick late. *Mitigation*: shared spike item (h); the Adapter's tests assert only the order of its own calls, and a one-tick-later landing degrades latency, not correctness.
- **R2. Warp, confinement and cursor units on a real letterboxed window.** If `warp_mouse` is not visible in the same frame, or emits a motion event, the zoom edge could nudge aim by a few units. *Mitigation*: PC-INPUT-SPIKE-1 (a), (b); the stored-`cursor_off` step already makes the warp frame independent of the OS read; acceptance of § 6.3 is gated on the spike.
- **R3. The `-1` wildcard may not match on a real SDL3 pad.** *Mitigation*: spike (f), (g); fallback is a per-device binding rebuilt on `joy_connection_changed`, behind `BindingFactory`, with no change to callers.
- **R4. `_input` plus `set_input_as_handled()` could collide with ADR-0030's focus design** (a `Control` expecting `ui_accept`). *Mitigation*: the layer is specified to take MenuInput only (TR-charttable-010); an amendment path is open (OQ-B); no `ui_*` action is read by gameplay or MenuInput.
- **R5. The registry exception for avatar tick-stepped loops** could be copied by other presenters. *Mitigation*: it is scoped to `AvatarFrames` and recorded as a foundation ask; ADR-0009's presenter tests assert that no other presenter reads `frame.T` for phase.
- **R6. PC-14 and the TR-pc-035 reading rest on ADR-0015.** If Body's transfer mutators do not reset `pos_prev` and `sub`, the arrival cell can be displaced. *Mitigation*: stated as an assumption on ADR-0015 and tested by the transfer property test (TR-shipbody-048).
- **R7. Frame-old `f_q`.** At a high turn rate while moving, aim could trail by up to the one-frame follow change. *Mitigation*: the GDD already bounds the follow term at 36 px and measures target acquisition in the motion-integrity spike; the Adapter does not add to the bound.
- **R8. Float `atan2` is not bit-identical across machines.** *Mitigation*: not claimed; the simulation replays the recorded submission log, and the Adapter-level trace test is per-machine.
- **R9. Solo detection for `give_up` is a row count.** If co-op seats exist without avatars, the count could mis-read. *Mitigation*: OQ-C; the check moves to a kernel session fact under ADR-0032.
- **R10. Action ids in rebinding files.** A renamed action would orphan a user override. *Mitigation*: stable integer ids with an append-only ledger (ADR-0007 § 3), names are display only.
- **R11. Touch, gyro and `VirtualJoystick` (4.7) are out of scope.** A later platform could need a fourth device class. *Mitigation*: `DeviceClass.OTHER` is ignored and adding a class is an enum append plus one classifier branch.

## GDD Requirements Addressed

Every row is by TR-ID (text in `docs/architecture/tr-registry.yaml`). "Covered" means this ADR decides its whole share; the Planned-ADR column of `requirements-traceability.md` is authoritative for who owns the rest. Count: 35 covered, 7 partial, 20 owned elsewhere (62 rows).

## Performance Implications
- **CPU**: Adapter at most 0.1 ms per frame, `controller.step` at most 0.02 ms per actor per tick, Avatar Presenter at most 0.1 ms per avatar per frame, diagnostics at most 0.01 ms per tick (TR-pc-029, advisory, release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK; none measured yet). `_input` does one `InputMap.event_is_action` per registered action for key, button and pad events (a few dozen compares, no allocation) and none for mouse motion. `controller.step` and the Adapter allocate nothing per call by construction (preallocated rings, rows, parallel arrays, a caller-owned `ChannelRef`), checked by the HOT-01 rule once the tooling lands.
- **Memory**: a handful of preallocated rings (edges, results, pre-play, menu events) sized by data; one `ControllerRow` per seat of 27 ints; `AdapterViews` and the ledgers are single objects. No per-frame allocation.
- **Load Time**: Four small tables under `assets/data/input/` load with the ADR-0007 pipeline at start-up; `BindingFactory` registers a few dozen actions once.
- **Network**: Intents at most 26 commands a second per player (VS-B); `controller.state` replicates as `SHARED_SUMMARY`; aim is not coarsened below the facing hysteresis.

content.content:
### Alternative 1: One `Controller` node that reads devices, owns the state and draws the body
- **Description**: A single `Node2D` (or autoload) reads `Input`, holds facing, gait and carry in its own fields, and moves the sprite.
- **Pros**: Least code; no read views; no resync because there is no boundary.
- **Cons**: State lives in the scene tree, so a save cannot restore it and a MIRROR peer cannot draw a remote body from state; presentation would write the simulation (kernel H4); the simulation would depend on a `Node` (ADR-0010 `SIM-01`); input timing would be the scene's, not the tick's.
- **Rejection Reason**: Breaks three Foundation rules and the GDD's PC-1 rationale; the three-part split is the minimum that satisfies them.

### Alternative 2: Fold the Controller Sim into Ship Body (one block, one hook)
- **Description**: Body owns intent, gait, facing and position; the Controller is only an Adapter and a Presenter.
- **Pros**: One fewer block and hook; no `controller.step` -> `body.integrate` ordering edge.
- **Cons**: Intent and facing are seat semantics (what the player asked for) read by Interaction, Attention, Horror and the HUD; position is a kinematic fact. Merging them couples every reader of the first to Body's schema and its restore rules, and the GDD rejected it for that reason (PC-1 rationale).
- **Rejection Reason**: Keeping the input record apart from the integrator keeps both restore contracts small; the cost is one hook edge, which the topo-sort already handles.

### Alternative 3: The Controller owns position and calls the Layout projection
- **Description**: `controller.step` integrates the foot box against Layout's rectangles.
- **Pros**: One owner for "where the player is".
- **Cons**: Puts the Layout projection inside an input system; cannot own an actor that transfers between bodies (pod hop, detach) without learning Body's rebase rules; Horror's reuse of `LocomotionStep` would have to reach into the Controller.
- **Rejection Reason**: PC-14's reasons; the composite ship and the transfer mutators are Body's.

### Alternative 4: Per-tick held-state commands instead of change-based intents
- **Description**: The Adapter submits the current octant and aim every tick; no change filter, no `last_acked`, no resync.
- **Pros**: Self-healing; no resync rule; the simulation can never disagree with the hands for more than a tick.
- **Cons**: A steady 60 or more commands a second against `MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK` and the `var_to_bytes` size check, for a state that is constant most of the time; the command log and the replay trace would be dominated by repeats; ADR-0002's coalescing exists for exactly the bursty case, not a firehose.
- **Rejection Reason**: Change-based submission with one resync rule has the same invariant (hands equal intent within a tick of `RUNNING`) at one fiftieth of the traffic, and the five triggers are all observable.

### Alternative 5: Poll-only edges, or latch in `_unhandled_input`
- **Description**: Use `is_action_just_pressed` and `just_released` for every edge; or latch events in `_unhandled_input`.
- **Pros**: Poll-only is the simplest code and needs no ring. `_unhandled_input` leaves `Control`s first refusal.
- **Cons**: Probe 6: a same-frame press and release cannot be ordered by polling, which the latch-until-released, fresh-press and hold-cancel rules need. `_unhandled_input` misses an event a focused `Control` consumed, which would silently drop a MenuInput accept.
- **Rejection Reason**: Ordered edges from `_input`, plus a poll for continuous state, is the smallest scheme that is correct for all three; the cost is the `EdgeRing`.

### Alternative 6: A custom binding layer instead of `InputMap`
- **Description**: The Adapter matches raw `InputEventKey`/`JoypadButton` records against its own table; no `InputMap` actions.
- **Pros**: No dependence on `InputMap` device semantics (probe 3); total control of conflicts and contexts.
- **Cons**: Re-implements modifier matching, axis deadzones, echo and per-device merging that the engine already provides; the HUD, Settings and accessibility screens would each need the custom layer; Godot's merging of devices per action (a held pad `interact` survives a touch of the mouse) would have to be rebuilt.
- **Rejection Reason**: `InputMap` with runtime registration, zero engine deadzone and the any-device wildcard gives the same control with the engine's matching; the pitfall (probe 3) is closed by one factory and one test.

### Alternative 7: Mouse aim through the camera pose (`mouse_to_world_view`) or anchored on the avatar
- **Description**: Use the full `pose_q` inverse for aim, or measure aim from the drawn avatar position.
- **Pros**: Matches picking and pings; the anchored form holds the beam rigid against the hand.
- **Cons**: `pose_q` contains the look-ahead `L`, which is a function of aim, so a still cursor would drift the beam (a feedback loop with no cursor drawn to explain it). Anchoring on the avatar puts the hidden-cursor reference up to the follow lag plus the look-ahead off the drawn avatar (GDD PC-5, ruling R4).
- **Rejection Reason**: The open-loop `f_q` form is the ruled one and ADR-0008 publishes it; the lint `CTL-06` keeps the loop open.

### Alternative 8: Identify devices by number (`device == 0`, or the `DEVICE_ID_*` constants)
- **Description**: Decide keyboard, mouse or pad from `event.device`.
- **Pros**: One integer compare.
- **Cons**: 4.7 changed the keyboard and mouse numbers and some pads already used 0 (`modules/input.md`); pads are numbered by enumeration order, so a pad that is not first matches nothing; a comparison with a constant bakes the engine's numbering into game code.
- **Rejection Reason**: Event type is stable across versions; the only legal numeric use is a variable holding the active pad's index, never a literal.

### Alternative 9: Persist the context, `last_acked` and the pre-play ledger
- **Description**: Save Adapter state so a load resumes mid-intent.
- **Pros**: A restore could keep the exact held input.
- **Cons**: The hands are the source of truth, not the save; a persisted `last_acked` would claim the simulation holds a value it just lost; the context is presentation. It would also put device state into a hashed block.
- **Rejection Reason**: The restore normalises transient fields and the resync re-sends the real hands (TR-pc-021).

## Consequences

### Positive
- Only five files can read a device; every other Controller file is pure over ints, so the Adapter's logic is unit-testable with a scripted source and replayable from a recorded trace.
- The Adapter cannot write the simulation by construction (no `ModuleFacet`, a `PresentationFacet` of class `INPUT_SURFACE`, an import-edge matrix that stops at `views/`), and the Controller Sim cannot read a device (no `Input` token is legal under `src/sim/`).
- One field list drives the block, the view and the snapshot, so the three cannot drift; a new field is one edit and one failing test until the rest follow.
- The 4.7 device-id change is closed twice: by classification on event type and by a literal-compare lint; the wildcard binding closes the pad-index hazard the probes found.
- Resync is one mechanism with five labelled causes, all observable from the clock, the result ring, the notifications and Body's view, with no kernel hook.
- Hold, toggle, pad and keyboard policies differ only in when the Adapter submits two commands the owners already define.
- Intent submission is ten to fifty times lighter than per-tick held state and stays inside the 26 commands a second budget.

### Negative
- Adapter state is lost on a restore and rebuilt from the hands; a player holding a key across a load gets one resend, at most one sub-pixel `sub` remainder, and no more.
- The Adapter reads the previous frame's `f_q` and layout (it runs before the pipeline), so aim and the zoom warp carry one frame of lag, and a warp frame drops one frame of mouse motion.
- Edge ordering needs an `EdgeRing` and a second path beside polling; the lint and fixtures to keep that honest are real work.
- The avatar's tick-stepped frames (idle, work, stagger, down) use the committed tick, an exception to a registry rule that must be defended in review and by test, because no lint can see it.
- Four Controller mutators are Class A in ADR-0003's vocabulary while the GDD says Class B; two documents must be amended.
- The Presenter and Audio share one pure function, which makes `AvatarFrames` a small cross-presentation contract that must stay stable.

## Risks
- **R1. Process order on a release export is unverified (KRN-LAT-02).** If the Adapter does not run before the driver, an intent sampled in frame N lands a tick late. *Mitigation*: shared spike item (h); the Adapter's tests assert only the order of its own calls, and a one-tick-later landing degrades latency, not correctness.
- **R2. Warp, confinement and cursor units on a real letterboxed window.** If `warp_mouse` is not visible in the same frame, or emits a motion event, the zoom edge could nudge aim by a few units. *Mitigation*: PC-INPUT-SPIKE-1 (a), (b); the stored-`cursor_off` step already makes the warp frame independent of the OS read; acceptance of § 6.3 is gated on the spike.
- **R3. The `-1` wildcard may not match on a real SDL3 pad.** *Mitigation*: spike (f), (g); fallback is a per-device binding rebuilt on `joy_connection_changed`, behind `BindingFactory`, with no change to callers.
- **R4. `_input` plus `set_input_as_handled()` could collide with ADR-0030's focus design** (a `Control` expecting `ui_accept`). *Mitigation*: the layer is specified to take MenuInput only (TR-charttable-010); an amendment path is open (OQ-B); no `ui_*` action is read by gameplay or MenuInput.
- **R5. The registry exception for avatar tick-stepped loops** could be copied by other presenters. *Mitigation*: it is scoped to `AvatarFrames` and recorded as a foundation ask; ADR-0009's presenter tests assert that no other presenter reads `frame.T` for phase.
- **R6. PC-14 and the TR-pc-035 reading rest on ADR-0015.** If Body's transfer mutators do not reset `pos_prev` and `sub`, the arrival cell can be displaced. *Mitigation*: stated as an assumption on ADR-0015 and tested by the transfer property test (TR-shipbody-048).
- **R7. Frame-old `f_q`.** At a high turn rate while moving, aim could trail by up to the one-frame follow change. *Mitigation*: the GDD already bounds the follow term at 36 px and measures target acquisition in the motion-integrity spike; the Adapter does not add to the bound.
- **R8. Float `atan2` is not bit-identical across machines.** *Mitigation*: not claimed; the simulation replays the recorded submission log, and the Adapter-level trace test is per-machine.
- **R9. Solo detection for `give_up` is a row count.** If co-op seats exist without avatars, the count could mis-read. *Mitigation*: OQ-C; the check moves to a kernel session fact under ADR-0032.
- **R10. Action ids in rebinding files.** A renamed action would orphan a user override. *Mitigation*: stable integer ids with an append-only ledger (ADR-0007 § 3), names are display only.
- **R11. Touch, gyro and `VirtualJoystick` (4.7) are out of scope.** A later platform could need a fourth device class. *Mitigation*: `DeviceClass.OTHER` is ignored and adding a class is an enum append plus one classifier branch.

## Performance Implications
- **CPU**: Adapter at most 0.1 ms per frame, `controller.step` at most 0.02 ms per actor per tick, Avatar Presenter at most 0.1 ms per avatar per frame, diagnostics at most 0.01 ms per tick (TR-pc-029, advisory, release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK; none measured yet). `_input` does one `InputMap.event_is_action` per registered action for key, button and pad events (a few dozen compares, no allocation) and none for mouse motion. `controller.step` and the Adapter allocate nothing per call by construction (preallocated rings, rows, parallel arrays, a caller-owned `ChannelRef`), checked by the HOT-01 rule once the tooling lands.
- **Memory**: a handful of preallocated rings (edges, results, pre-play, menu events) sized by data; one `ControllerRow` per seat of 27 ints; `AdapterViews` and the ledgers are single objects. No per-frame allocation.
- **Load Time**: Four small tables under `assets/data/input/` load with the ADR-0007 pipeline at start-up; `BindingFactory` registers a few dozen actions once.
- **Network**: Intents at most 26 commands a second per player (VS-B); `controller.state` replicates as `SHARED_SUMMARY`; aim is not coarsened below the facing hysteresis.

content.thinking:
Testing both orderings confirms `_input` follows reverse tree order regardless of priority values — priority doesn't affect its ordering at all, only sibling position does.

This reveals a real latching gotcha: the ADR's guarantee breaks silently if any later-in-tree node (HUD, debug overlay, dev tools) calls `set_input_as_handled()` before reaching the adapter, since the ADR never specifies required tree position. I'd flag this as an amendment need — composition root should place `InputAdapter` as the last child of root to guarantee it runs first — and mark it non-blocking but a major finding, since it only causes missed presses conditionally rather than universally.

Checking FakeInputSource against the abstract interface, it correctly implements all ten required methods. I'm also scanning through a batch of other potential engine gotchas — gamepad events under varying max_fps, fractional mouse warping with DPI scaling, confined/hidden mouse mode on Windows with letterbox, mouse motion polling vs events, joypad connection signals at boot, and action strength with exact_match defaults for modifier-key combos like Shift+W — most of which check out fine against the ADR's design.

Now I'm looking at physical keycode handling for layout independence (confirming KEY_1 digit bindings work regardless of AZERTY vs QWERTY), IME/AltGr edge cases, mouse button aliasing for interact actions, wheel-as-action zoom bindings, and error logging for undefined actions — all consistent with expectations. I'm tallying which of the twelve probes were actually reproduced versus just assumed plausible: probes 1, 2, 3, 6, 7 (partially, since it relied on timing through await), and 10 were verified, while probe 10 specifically only confirms storage and not actual behavior.

I'm also confirming that parse_input_event only takes effect after a flush, consistent with the stated claim, and checking that DisplayServer's headless stub still exposes keyboard_get_label_from_physical. Then I'm examining the real device ID issue — since physical keyboard events in this Godot version report device 16, I need to verify that the BindingFactory normalizes rebinding captures to device ANY rather than locking to a specific physical device, which becomes a new minor finding (E7) about ensuring captured rebinds go through factory normalization and considering how device IDs affect InputMap.action_has_event.

I'm scanning for Object method name clashes across the Key Interfaces and finding none, so I'll log this as a low-severity informational finding confirming typed returns are fine and nothing blocks the build. I also verify a few more signatures are correctly typed, confirm that integer and StringName constants are safe, and check that packed arrays like snapshots are properly duplicated rather than passed by reference before glancing at MenuInputQueue's column exposures.

Checking the queue's private field columns, there's no setter exposed, which lines up with ADR-0004's rule against property setters for these fields, so no issue there either. I'm also noting that process_mode and time_scale usage for the hit-stop adapter look fine, but flagging a possible gotcha around window focus loss on Windows breaking confined mouse mode -- I'll mark this as an unverified, non-blocking finding recommending cursor mode be re-asserted on focus-in and pause transitions, since the engine or OS might silently drop confinement. I'm about to note a related concern about embedded game windows or Steam Deck behavior.

Grouping this with warp/confine platform support: Input.warp_mouse is only documented as supported on Windows, macOS, and Linux, with no effect on Android/iOS/Web, and Wayland behavior remains unverified. Since Steam Deck runs Linux (via gamescope), I think the ADR's spike matrix should explicitly add a Deck test case alongside the windowed editor and release export spikes already planned.

Now I'm looking at cross-ADR dependencies: ADR-0001's claim that `_input` fires before `_process` needs clarification, since `_input` delivery order actually follows tree order rather than process_priority, meaning the composition root must position the Adapter correctly relative to other `_input` consumers -- this should be called out either in ADR-0001 or folded into ADR-0009's INPUT_SURFACE rule. I'm also starting to look at what ADR-0015 needs to expose through BodyView.

Also checking ADR-0010's READ-01 symbol list against ADR-0019 — it's missing tokens like `Viewport.warp_mouse`, `get_mouse_position`, `DisplayServer.keyboard_get_label_from_physical`, `NOTIFICATION_APPLICATION_FOCUS_OUT`, `joy_connection_changed`, and various `MOUSE_MODE_*` constants. I should flag that `set_input_as_handled` needs to be added to the symbol list and allow-list too, since it's an input-related token currently missing.

I'm confirming ADR-0006's dictionary snapshot keys are fine as strings, then settling on an overall verdict — leaning toward "CONCERNS (1 blocking)" given the deadzone registration issue (E1, blocking/high).

I'm also drafting E2: a major non-blocking finding that `_input` dispatch order follows reverse tree order rather than process_priority, meaning the Adapter could miss events already consumed by other `_input` nodes deeper in the tree. My proposed fix is to require the Adapter be placed as the last child of the root (or asserted as composition-root), restrict `set_input_as_handled` calls for gameplay keys to the Adapter only, and add a test covering this ordering behavior.

E3 catches that `set_input_as_handled()` should be called on the viewport, not as a bare Node method. E4 flags that deriving edges from `event_is_action` doesn't work for JoypadMotion events, since every motion event above the deadzone reports as pressed, causing duplicate detections and ring buffer overflow — I'm keeping this as its own finding rather than folding it into E1 for traceability. E5 covers warp/confine mode support across platforms and re-asserting on focus return, marked non-blocking and unverified. E6 raises whether the engine synthesizes release events on focus-out through `_input`, and whether the ADR's claim that GDScript lacks `Input.release_pressed_events` justifies the Adapter maintaining its own ledger.

Then I move through E7 (mouse wheel notches emit press+release pairs, so I should only use pressed events, plus handling horizontal wheel and touchpad gestures which get classified as OTHER and safely ignored), E8 (rebind capture needs to normalize device index via the factory, dropping pressed/echo flags), E9 (verifying that FakeInputSource/EngineInputSource must fully implement all ten abstract methods with explicit returns on every path, confirmed partial overrides are a parse error), and E10 beginning a plausibility probe.

For E10/E11 I'm examining the claim that device -1 is a "coincidence" matching DEVICE_ID_EMULATION -- my probing actually confirms -1 is the engine's genuine all-devices wildcard (what the editor itself writes into project.godot), so I should flag that "coincidence" framing as unnecessary and mark the ALL_DEVICES constant naming as unverified, folding this correction into E10's info note. The pause-silence input handling and the viewport mouse-position-after-warp behavior both check out fine, so now I'm ready to write out the concrete amendment text.

input.verdict: CONCERNS (1 blocking: E1). Idiomatic overall for 4.7.2: `_input` latch plus `_process` poll, runtime `InputMap` registration, `physical_keycode`, event-type device classification, `@abstract` ports, typed collections and caller-owned buffers all hold up. Re-probed headless on 4.7.2 and CONFIRMED probes 1, 2, 3 (-1 wildcard matches pad 2 and keyboard 5; a pad-0 binding does not match pad 2), 6 (same-frame press+release leaves just_pressed and just_released true and pressed false) and 10 (deadzone stored). Also confirmed that `_input` runs before the frame's `_process` with press/release order preserved (supports ADR-0001 § 3 item 3b). Probes 4, 5, 8, 9, 11 and 12 were not re-run but are plausible. Probe 10 only shows the 0.0 is stored, not what it does, and that behaviour is the E1 bug. Every window, warp, focus, wheel, SDL3 and release-export claim is correctly marked UNVERIFIED and gated on PC-INPUT-SPIKE-1.

findings.text: § 3.3 registers every action with `InputMap.add_action(name, 0.0)` and says this makes `MOVE_DEADZONE` and `AIM_DEADZONE` the only deadzones. Probed on 4.7.2: with a 0.0 deadzone an `InputEventJoypadMotion` with axis_value 0.0 reports `is_action_pressed` TRUE for both the positive and the negative direction action, because the engine's same-direction test accepts a zero value and `abs(0.0) >= 0.0`. A tiny 0.02 value is also 'pressed'. A trigger axis at rest (value 0.0) reports its action pressed. `Input.is_action_pressed` goes true for both `mv_r` and `mv_l` after one centred-stick event, while `get_action_raw_strength` correctly stays 0.0. Effects: `is_action_down` / `Input.is_action_pressed` is wrong for any action with a pad axis or trigger binding (move, aim, NAV, a trigger-bound run or interact); the `_input` edge latch records press edges for centred sticks and never sees a release, which breaks latch-until-released (§ 4.3), the hold-mode cancel, the resync comparison of the real `interact` state, and fills the EdgeRing. Probe 10 verified only that 0.0 is stored. The deadzone is not needed to keep raw strength raw: `get_action_raw_strength` ignores it.
findings.amendment: Replace 'zero engine deadzone' with a non-zero deadzone for every catalogue action (engine default 0.5, or the existing 0.2) and keep `MOVE_DEADZONE` / `AIM_DEADZONE` as Adapter-level scalings over `get_action_raw_strength`. Amend § 3.3, Alternative 6 and probe 10 ('stores 0.0') accordingly. Add a BindingFactory test: a centred JoypadMotion (0.0) and a trigger at rest do not make any action pressed, and `InputMap.action_get_deadzone` is never 0.0. Add a headless probe 13 with the p1 script: centred-stick event and trigger-at-rest, asserting both are not pressed.

findings.text: § 3.1 and § 3.2 treat the Adapter as the single `_input` latch, and § 3.2 / R4 / OQ-B have it call `set_input_as_handled()` in `chart_table`. Probed: `_input` is delivered in REVERSE TREE ORDER (a later sibling first) and `process_priority` has no effect on `_input` order. Two nodes were tested, with the priorities swapped between runs, and the later sibling always received the event first and, when it handled it, the earlier sibling never saw it. `process_priority` -100 therefore orders only the Adapter's `_process`. Any node later in the tree that handles an event first (the Chart Table layer, HUD, the ADR-0031 debug overlay and `DevInputSink`) silently starves the Adapter's ring, which is a missed press with no error. `set_input_as_handled()` does not change `Input.*` poll state (actions update before dispatch), so only the ring is affected.
findings.amendment: State in § 3.1 that the composition root adds `InputAdapter` as the LAST child of the root so its `_input` runs first, and add a boot assertion plus a two-node unit test (copy of the probe). State that only the Adapter may call `set_input_as_handled()` for action-bound events, and that the dev overlay latches through the Adapter's `DevInputSink` rather than its own `_input`. Record in ADR-0001 § 3 item 3b that `_input` ordering is tree order, not priority.

findings.text: § 3.2, R4 and OQ-B write `set_input_as_handled()` as if it were a Node method. Probed: a Node script calling `set_input_as_handled()` is a parse error ('Function not found in base self'); the method is `Viewport.set_input_as_handled()`. `get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()` compiles and works from `_input`. The § 8.1 READ-01 symbol list also omits this token and the other device-adjacent engine members used in `EngineInputSource` (`get_mouse_position`, `warp_mouse`, `joy_connection_changed`, `NOTIFICATION_APPLICATION_FOCUS_OUT`, `NOTIFICATION_WM_WINDOW_FOCUS_OUT`).
findings.amendment: Write `get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()` everywhere. Add `set_input_as_handled` to the § 8.1 symbol list (allowed only in `input_adapter.gd`), and decide whether the focus notifications and `joy_connection_changed` belong to the allow-listed files only.

findings.text: § 3.2 records 'a press or release of a registered action (resolved with `InputMap.event_is_action`)' for every device event. For `InputEventJoypadMotion`, `is_action_pressed` is true on EVERY motion event while the stick is past the deadzone (probed: successive 0.7 and 0.9 events both report pressed). The ring would receive a duplicate 'press' per motion event per axis per frame, never a release record, which is an overflow and ordering hazard (`PC_EDGE_OVERFLOW` fail-safe becomes the normal path while a stick is held).
findings.amendment: Have `RawEvent.classify` treat `InputEventJoypadMotion` as continuous-only: no edge records. Derive stick and trigger edges (NAV, MOVE_DEADZONE crossings, trigger-bound actions) in the Adapter from `get_action_raw_strength` with the existing hysteresis, once per frame. Keep edge records for key, mouse button and joypad button events only, and de-duplicate against an Adapter held-set.

findings.text: § 4.4 and § 6.3 depend on `MOUSE_MODE_CONFINED_HIDDEN`, `Input.set_mouse_mode` applied only on change, and `warp_mouse`. Not covered by the spike matrix and UNVERIFIED: (1) the docs restrict `warp_mouse` to Windows, macOS and Linux, and Wayland is a doubtful case; the budgets target RM-DECK, which is Linux. The spike lists only an editor session and a release export, not the Deck or gamescope. (2) The editor's embedded game window (4.4+) may not honour confine or warp, so a spike run in the embedded window would give false results. (3) If the OS drops confinement on focus loss or alt-tab, 'apply only on change' never re-applies it. `Input.warp_mouse` takes window coordinates and `Viewport.warp_mouse` takes viewport coordinates; they are equal only because the root has no stretch.
findings.amendment: Add to PC-INPUT-SPIKE-1: run (a), (b) and (e) on RM-DECK (Linux) and in a non-embedded window. Make `EngineInputSource` re-assert the cursor mode on every FOCUS_IN and PAUSED->RUNNING, not only on change. Specify the fallback when `warp_cursor` is a no-op: keep the stored `cursor_off` as a virtual cursor (accumulated `InputEventMouseMotion.relative`) so zoom and handover do not depend on warp. Name `Input.warp_mouse` (window pixels) as the one call used.

findings.text: § 3.7 says the Adapter keeps its own held ledger because `Input.release_pressed_events` is not exposed to GDScript (probe 9, plausible). The engine is believed to call it internally on main-window focus-out (UNVERIFIED), which would deliver synthetic release events through `_input` after the Adapter has already zeroed intents. `NOTIFICATION_APPLICATION_FOCUS_OUT` is app-level (alt-tab to another app); a window drag or an OS modal dialog may only fire `NOTIFICATION_WM_WINDOW_FOCUS_OUT` or `Window.focus_exited`. That is already spike (e).
findings.amendment: Make release records for controls absent from the held ledger idempotent in the ring (no error, no counter), and have the focus handler connect all three signals and notifications to one latch. Record in spike (e) whether synthetic releases arrive via `_input`.

findings.text: § 3.2 and § 6.4 latch 'a mouse wheel notch with its sign'. A wheel is an `InputEventMouseButton` (WHEEL_UP / WHEEL_DOWN) delivered as a press immediately followed by a release; wheel events are not coalesced by `use_accumulated_input`; the wheel has a fractional `factor` on high-resolution wheels and precision touchpads, and horizontal wheel buttons also exist. A latch that counts both the press and the release, or ignores `factor`, double counts. Touchpad gestures arrive as `InputEventPanGesture` / `InputEventMagnifyGesture`, which classify as OTHER and are ignored (acceptable, but the user-visible effect on touchpads should be stated).
findings.amendment: Count only `pressed == true` wheel events, sum signs, ignore the paired release, ignore `factor` for the sign (one step per frame is already capped by § 6.4), and state that gesture events are ignored. Record the burst size in spike (c).

findings.text: § 3.3 builds every binding with `device = -1`, and user rebinds go through BindingFactory. Probed: a fresh `InputEventKey` carries device 16 and a mouse button 32, and real captured events carry the real device (or pad index). If the Settings rebind capture stores the captured event directly, the new binding is device-specific, which is the probe-3 trap again.
findings.amendment: Specify that the rebind capture path duplicates the captured event, sets `device = BINDING_ANY_DEVICE` and clears `pressed` / `echo` before `action_add_event`. Extend the § 8.3 factory test to cover user-capture events as well as the defaults.

findings.text: 4.7 typed-return rule and ports. `@abstract` on its own line before `class_name` / `extends`, with `@abstract func ... -> T` bodies, compiles on 4.7.2 (probed). A subclass that implements only some abstract methods is a parse error (probed), so `FakeInputSource` and `EngineInputSource` must implement all ten. Under the 4.7 override rule an override that omits its return annotation inherits the typed return and must return on every path, so a stub like `func cursor_px(): pass` fails. The fallback 'plain base class with `push_error` stubs' must also return a value. Typed `static func fields() -> Array[Dictionary]` over a `const ROWS: Array[Dictionary]` literal compiled and ran (probed); const arrays and dictionaries are read-only, which suits the schema list.
findings.amendment: Add to Implementation Guidelines: ports are `@abstract`, every override restates its return type and returns on every path (add `return 0` / `return Vector2i.ZERO` stubs in the Fake), and the lint pack flags an override without a return annotation. No Object-method name clash was found: the `get_*` accessors on `ControllerView`, `AdapterViews` and `MenuInputQueue`, `count()`, `clear()`, `setup()` and `on_result()` do not shadow Object or Node members.

findings.text: Plausibility notes. (a) § 3.3 calls `BINDING_ANY_DEVICE == InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_EMULATION` 'a coincidence'. Probed behaviour is that -1 is the engine's any-device binding wildcard (pad-0 binding misses pad 2; -1 matches pads 0 and 2 and keyboards 16 and 5), and 4.7.2 reports DEVICE_ID_EMULATION -1, KEYBOARD 16, MOUSE 32. The code does not depend on the equality, so this is harmless. (b) § 6.1 `floor(pos_curr)` on a `Vector2i` is legal and returns a `Vector2i` (probed) but is a no-op, and ADR-0015 exposes Body position as scalar getters (`pos_x`, `pos_y`), not a `Vector2i`. (c) Probe 12 (root `content_scale_mode` 0 in a bare script) says nothing about the project; ADR-0008 owns the stretch setting, and the 4.7 stretch default change applies to new-project templates only. (d) Packed-array columns (`snapshot`, `MenuInputQueue`) are safe: PackedArrays are reference types, § 2.7 duplicates them, and the 4.7 element-write-skips-setter change is irrelevant because the design forbids property setters (ADR-0004).
findings.amendment: Reword (a) to 'the engine's any-device wildcard; the code depends only on the constant'. Drop `floor()` in § 6.1 or restate it against ADR-0015's getter shape.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0001 § 3 item 3b says `_input` / `_unhandled_input` are delivered before the frame's `_process` (UNVERIFIED), and ADR-0009's INPUT_SURFACE rule says a holder latches intents from events. Probed on 4.7.2 headless: `_input` is delivered before `_process` with press/release order preserved (confirmed), but `_input` order among nodes is reverse tree order and ignores `process_priority`. A later-in-tree node that handles an event starves the Adapter's ring. ADR-0001 § 3 and ADR-0009 imply that priority governs the Adapter's whole input path.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0001 § 3: mark 3b probed (headless), add 'process_priority orders `_process` only; `_input` order is reverse tree order'. ADR-0009 INPUT_SURFACE rule: the composition root adds each INPUT_SURFACE object as the last child of the root, and no other node calls `set_input_as_handled()` on action-bound events.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0019 § 1.1 lists a 'pod-body test' among the Controller's reads of `body.state`, and § 6.1 reads `pos_curr` as a `Vector2i` from Body's published view. ADR-0015 publishes scalar getters (`pos_x`, `pos_y`, `prev_x`, `prev_y`, `body_of_actor`, `seat_of_actor`, `actor_of_seat`, ...) and states the pod-body test is Layout's or Transit's, not Body's. cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0019 reads `pos_x` / `pos_y` (or builds the `Vector2i` once at the Adapter boundary) and sources the pod-body test from the owner ADR-0015 names. ADR-0015 confirms the getter names in its Key Interfaces.

If either node sits later in the tree and receives keyboard, mouse or pad events through its own `_input`, `_gui_input` or `ui_*` actions, it takes the event before the Adapter (E2).
